The hot file is EMPTY, which is the resting state this convention intends between sprints — the next sprint's items are authored fresh against the authority docs rather than inherited. (Sprint 17's own eleven items are RETAINED here by the merge of 2026-08-24: that sprint closed under the other reading of this note, with prose archived and metadata kept, and this merge does not re-archive another session's bookkeeping.)
Canonical backlog for Project Io — the authoritative METADATA index of every backlog item.
One item = one object in `items`.
STATUS (authoritative; JSON wins over any prose/glyph disagreement):
designed    (glyph ✓) — design settled, promote-ready.
design-owed (glyph ~) — design still owed; must be settled before promotion.
PRIORITY (ascending): F C B A S SSS.
F=deferred/parked, C=low, B=medium, A=important, S=high, SSS=do-immediately.
`parked:true` is the explicit flag for F-priority items.
DIFFICULTY (1-5): 1=~5min, 2=~20min, 3=~1h, 4=~3h, 5=~12h+ (break a 5 down).
SEQUENCING: `requires` lists BL-XXX ids of backlog items that must land first (supercedes the
old `waits_on` short_name list — v2 schema 2026-06-17). `blocked_on` names a truly-external
prerequisite with no backlog item (third-party dep, real-world gate). An item can be `designed`
and still have unmet `requires`. Both fields are nullable; [] means no dependencies.
WORKFLOW: a `designed` item is PROMOTED into REFINED.md and DELIVERED (see DELIVERY.md).
A `design-owed` item is DESIGNED first (prose settled in `design` field, status flipped).
When work lands, the item is RETAINED here under the terminal status `complete` with a
resolution/completion_note, and design propagates into the authority doc. (Convention updated
2026-07-04: terminal items were once removed; the tooling — gyre.py, progress counts — now
depends on them staying. Do not delete landed entries.)
(Terminal status normalised 2026-08-01: `complete` is the only one. `shipped` was a
synonym with no defined difference — written only by tools/session/ship_items.js and
apply_session_close.js, which now write `complete`; the six items carrying it were
converted. Readers still tolerate the old value, so nothing breaks on an old branch.)
DESIGN PROSE — the `design` field (policy updated 2026-06-17):
- ALL items: prose lives in the `design` field here, not in BACKLOG.md.
- NEW items: author prose here directly. No BACKLOG.md body.
- LEGACY items (pre-2026-06-17): `design: "@BACKLOG.md"` means prose is still in markdown.
Migrate to this field on first edit (design settle or promotion) — do not wait for promotion.
On migration: write prose here, replace the BACKLOG.md body with a tombstone line.
- ON PROMOTION into REFINED.md: delete any remaining BACKLOG.md body (if not yet migrated).
- BACKLOG.md therefore only drains, never grows, and is deleted once empty.
- For designs with rich tables use markdown in the `design` string (tables render fine).
- `design: "@<doc>"` is also valid as a pointer to an authority doc when prose lives there.
VERSION GOAL (policy added 2026-07-08): every NEW item names which version it is FOR via the
`version_goal` field — the minor it targets ("v0.0.9"), the next one ("v0.1.0"), or
"post-v0.1.0" for anything beyond the prototype's remaining arc (see ROADMAP.md for the
live version sequence and themes). This is a goal, not a promise — it may slip a version at
re-sequencing, same as priority. Legacy items predating this policy are not backfilled; treat
a missing `version_goal` as "unset (legacy)", not as "post-v0.1.0".
ARCHIVE — the hot/cold split (policy added 2026-08-02):
This file is the METADATA INDEX and is read ACROSS items far more often than INTO one.
So when an item lands, its narrative fields — design, resolution, completion_note,
progress_note — MOVE OUT to docs/development/archive/backlog-design-<quarter>.json.
The item keeps `design: "@<that path>"` (the pointer form blessed above) plus an
`archived` field naming the cold file. This is the authority time-slice made physical:
backlog.json owns the item while it is open; the cold store and the subject authority
doc own it once it has landed.
- Run it: tools/session/archive_designs.js (Delivery close step, after ship_items.js).
- Read it back: tools/session/backlog_query.js --full, or backlog_view.js — both resolve
the pointer transparently, so an archived item reads exactly like a hot one.
- Reverse it: archive_designs.js --restore [BL-XXX ...]. Nothing is ever deleted.
- AMEND A LANDED ITEM'S PROSE IN THE COLD FILE, not here — the hot file has no copy.
- backlog_lint.js FAILS on an `archived` pointer with no record behind it, and WARNS
when frozen history climbs back over 30% of this file.
AUTHOR (policy added 2026-08-22): items may carry an `author` field naming who
proposed the item (e.g. "Joe"). Informational only — no effect on status, priority,
or workflow. Nullable; missing/null means unattributed (legacy items). Design
brainstorms that haven't yet become a backlog item live in docs/development/design/.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Rivals buy firms too - buy_corporation joins the scored-utility candidate list
items.design: The symmetry half of BL-628 (whole-firm buyout), and a widening of the BL-202/BL-203 exception in its established shape: deterministic, seeded, scored-utility, a legal verb and never a planner. THE WORK: score buy_corporation in corp_ai.cpp's existing candidate list, capped at one acquisition per evaluation, its price carried in the candidate's spend under the solvency gate so a rival cannot buy itself below its reserve floor. Availability is gated on the target's ownership class, not on the acquirer's cash - the 'never on cash' ruling's shape. Record the grant in the standing rules with its date, as every prior widening is recorded. SAVING UP IS NOT PLANNING, and this item owns the distinction: Ben's Sprint 20 goal wants a corp to accumulate cash toward an acquisition, but a scorer that defers a cheap build today in order to afford a firm tomorrow is edging toward the planner the standing rules forbid. The honest route needs no new machinery - accumulation is EMERGENT when the buy candidate outscores the marginal build, since a tick with no affordable positive candidate simply banks its cash. Whether that actually happens at the authored weights is a measurement, and BL-634 (acquisition viability) is where it is taken.

items.author: Ben
items.title: The spawn shortlist - warm start in spectate, then seat the player on a viable corp at random
items.design: Design settled in CORPORATION_GENERATION.md § The spawn shortlist, and the seat, and STARTUP.md § The seat (Ben, 2026-08-26). THE WORK: move the 80-tick warm start ahead of seating and run it under corp_ai_params::spectating; shortlist the specialists clearing the viability floor (solvent at the end, trailing net over 8 quarters non-negative); draw one against the world seed and re-point is_player/player_entity. Remove app_screen::choosing_corp, draw_corp_choice_screen, build_corp_choices, apply_corp_choice, the Surprise me press, verify.show_corp_choice and scripts/verify/corp_choice.lua. THE COST, taken knowingly: every corp is scorer-driven through the warm start where the seated one used to be excluded, so every seed's opening moves and the goldens re-bless ONCE, in a single wave with dated provenance. player_seed_sweep --guard is re-pointed at the shortlist's properties. NOT SOLVED by this item: the shallow-opening distribution the old screen was built for - carried in the review queue. WEIGHTED DRAW (Ben, 2026-08-26, answering NR-649): 'mostly random for now, targeted towards population centres and processing, rather than extraction.' The floor filters; the draw over the shortlist is BIASED, never gated - a pure-extraction corp on thin ground stays drawable, just less often. Two weights, both off existing signals: a processor among the holdings weights up (the depth lever the viability floor cannot provide), and holdings on or near populated ground weight up. The weights are a first cut; player_seed_sweep REPORTS the resulting distribution rather than asserting it against a target.

items.title: The acquisition loop is the sprint's definition of done - measure it, then move the constants
items.design: Ben's goal for Sprint 20, stated 2026-08-26: 'corporations can save up in a few economy ticks to buy another company, and then continue making a profit.' That is a MEASURABLE loop and this item is the instrument for it - a headless harness over world/*, run past the warm start, asserting three things in order: (1) a seated corp's balance climbs rather than bleeds, (2) it reaches the price of the cheapest buyable public firm within a stated number of quarters, (3) its net is still positive N quarters AFTER the acquisition, with the acquired holdings folded in. Measured relative across seeds on a fixed rival field, per the spawn-viability pass's own rule - absolute numbers are confounded by the open economy pathologies. k_acquisition_multiple is CALIBRATED from what this measures, never guessed: measure first, then move the constant, and never weaken an assertion to make it pass. The harness is the deliverable, not a one-off script - it gets a skill entry under verifier-headless.

items.author: Ben
items.title: The household basket ladders by ERA as well as by stratum
items.design: Design in POPULATION.md section Population demand and MARKETS.md section Demand channels. THE MEASURED CAUSE: population_demand's basket names food_rations, agricultural_produce, water, clean_water, consumer_goods, medical_supplies - and three of those six are made by NO ancient recipe, so a 0 CE campaign has three household goods. Recipes have carried an era field since BL-433; the demand baskets never did. THE WORK: band the basket the same way and author the ancient rows - ceramics, cloth, leather, dressed_stone - which are exactly the terminal artisan goods the ancient roster produces and nothing currently buys. Compose with the stratum ladder POPULATION.md already calls for: era decides WHICH value chain, stratum decides how far up it. This one item resurrects four of the seven ancient dead ends. SCOPE GREW, from BL-648's measurement (2026-08-26): this item also owns chain_depth's R1b list, and R1b hides a SECOND red list of the same defect class as the one BL-648 names. Neither inject_population_demand nor inject_background_demand is era-gated, so an ancient campaign genuinely 'wants' silicon, machinery, alloys and electronics - goods only the industrial arc can make - and R1b's hand-narrowed list quietly absorbs that. Banding the baskets is what makes R1b derivable from the injector registry instead of hand-maintained, so the two halves land together: band the demand, then let R1b read the banded truth. BL-648's agent deliberately did NOT fold this in, to avoid burying the ten goods that item exists to name - the right call, and it makes this item bigger than it looked when minted. THE MAGNITUDE, measured by BL-649's census (2026-08-26): at 0 CE, inject_background_demand alone is 8,417.8 of 10,544.0 total modelled market demand - 79.8% - and FIVE OF ITS SIX GOODS cannot be produced in that band at all. Household adds 435.4 more on clean_water / consumer_goods / medical_supplies, likewise unmakeable. So 65.7% OF ALL 0 CE DEMAND NAMES GOODS THE ANCIENT BAND CANNOT MAKE. That is not a rounding error in a basket, it is most of the demand in the world pointing at nothing, and it is why the ancient economy reads as having almost no buyers. Note the corollary for the tuning passes: fixing this will move prices everywhere, so the census must be run before and after and the deltas kept. MOVED INTO SPRINT 20 (Ben, 2026-08-26): these are the two levers that actually move spawn viability, and Sprint 20 owns the viability question through BL-634. Built in the same session as the diagnosis so the census and spawn_solvency baselines are hours old rather than a sprint stale.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Industry becomes a consumer - a building's upkeep is credits AND goods
items.design: Design in FINANCE.md section Upkeep is credits AND goods - for buildings too. THE LARGEST STRUCTURAL SINK AVAILABLE, and it invents nothing: a unit already pays credits plus a goods vector through run_unit_upkeep, and a building pays credits only. That asymmetry is an omission, not a design. THE WORK: a per-building-type goods vector drawn against the owner's pool on the building's own body, in a fixed order (two buildings of one corp on one body draw the same stock and the order decides which goes short). The shortfall rule is the SAME rule - an unmet draw weakens the building by the same subtraction an out-of-supply unit takes; a factory short of tools runs badly, it does not vanish. Rates authored in economy.lua per building type, era-banded, every rate authorable at 0.0 so the SHAPE can land before the numbers are settled (the BL-454 precedent). Why it matters more than the others: demand then scales with how much industry exists, with no weight for anyone to maintain. MOVED INTO SPRINT 20 (Ben, 2026-08-26): these are the two levers that actually move spawn viability, and Sprint 20 owns the viability question through BL-634. Built in the same session as the diagnosis so the census and spawn_solvency baselines are hours old rather than a sprint stale. RATES STAY 0.0 UNTIL BL-654 LANDS (Ben, 2026-08-26). The measured collapse (227 -> 19 operating firms) is a consequence of drawing without bidding, not of the rate; BL-654's buy-with-a-ceiling is what makes a non-zero rate survivable, and the rate is then measured against the census and the operating-firm count rather than chosen.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Construction draws materials - in the opening years, and as centres grow
items.design: Ben, 2026-08-26: 'we need those first 20 years of generation to include construction'. MEASURED CONTEXT: materials are authored per building (resource_costs) and charged at the build press, but generation PLACES buildings rather than constructing them, so the draw never fires during the opening years - stone and timber have a construction sink on paper and no pull in practice. TWO HALVES, and the second is the one that lasts: (1) make the opening years actually build, so the warm start carries a real material pull; (2) make POPULATION CENTRES draw construction materials as they grow, which does not decay once the warm start ends. An ancient economy's largest material sink is building, and half (2) makes that structurally true rather than transiently.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Roads, ports and hubs draw materials to stay standing
items.design: The infrastructure demand channel (MARKETS.md section Demand channels). The logistics_maintenance budget line already exists and names exactly this, so the state half has a home. THE WORK: a network that consumes stone and timber to stay standing - a permanent sink scaled by GEOGRAPHY rather than by population, which is a shape none of the other channels has. Second-order and wanted: it gives reach a running cost, so extending the network becomes a decision rather than a ratchet. OWED: this item writes its paragraph into LOGISTICS.md; the design register in MARKETS.md points at it.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Government satellite launches - the tenth budget line, and space goods' first real buyer
items.design: Ben, 2026-08-26: 'add endpoints for space goods in government issued satellite launches'. Design in NATIONS.md section A budget. THE MACHINERY EXISTS - nations hold a weighted budget over priority lines, run_national_budget has claim/transfer machinery, and strategic_reserve is already a goods-buying line that no consumer claims on. THE WORK: a tenth line, space_programme, buying spacecraft_components and propellant through the BL-350 procurement seam (never on the open market - that is strategic_reserve's own rule). APPEND-ONLY: the weight vector is indexed by the enum and serialised, so the line goes last. Why it is worth more than a sink: state demand arrives in LUMPS and follows a weight a rival can lobby to move, so it is worth playing politics over rather than merely scaling into. ALSO OWNS spacecraft_components (BL-648's measurement, 2026-08-26): the guard's red list came back with ELEVEN goods, not the ten expected, and the eleventh is this one. Its exemption claimed BL-350 procurement, but procurement is a resource-agnostic TRANSFER between two corps' pools - it moves goods without consuming them, and admitting it as an injector would substantiate the entire roster at once. src/world contains no militia, and corp_ai.cpp says outright that the scorer does not emit those verbs today, so nothing automatic buys it. This line is its first real buyer.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Research consumes goods, not only credits
items.design: Ben, 2026-08-26: 'perhaps we could make research consume alternate goods as well'. Design written into RESEARCH.md. It gives the TOP of the production chain a buyer and turns the tech ladder into an economic decision rather than a free accumulator only time gates. Two properties: the basket is era-banded like every other, and a shortfall SLOWS research rather than voiding it (the same shape every goods draw takes). BLOCKED BY DESIGN on BL-619 (research system), which is a session with Ben - the rates, and whether the draw sits on the university or on the nation's budget lines, belong to that session rather than being settled ahead of it.

items.author: Ben
items.title: A battle consumes what it fires - conflict as a demand shock
items.design: The conflict demand channel (MARKETS.md section Demand channels). MEASURED: ordnance is priced at 43.00, near the top of the ancient roster, and its only draw is a per-head upkeep rate that BL-635's rescale took to 0.0035 - effectively nil. So the roster's most valuable military good has no buyer. THE WORK: a battle draws ordnance in proportion to what it commits, against the owner's pool, deterministically. WHY IT IS THE MOST INTERESTING OF THE EIGHT: it is the only channel that couples the game's two pillars - it makes Conflict move Trade, so a war somewhere else is a price signal here. OWED: this item writes its paragraph into MILITARY.md.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Tobacco, spices, coffee and furs get the buyer they were authored for
items.design: MEASURED: four endemic goods are on the roster, extractable, priced - and wanted by nothing at all, in any band. They pass the orphan check by naming 'mercantile demand', which BL-648 shows does not exist. THE WORK: a household demand that scales with WEALTH rather than headcount, flavoured by NATIONAL CHARACTER so different nations crave different luxuries. That asymmetry is the design, not a detail: it makes the trade route directional by construction - extract where it grows, sell where the money is - which is the most Trade-shaped channel of the eight and the one that most directly serves the pillar. Note it is also the first demand whose SIZE is a function of prosperity, so it rewards a player who has made somewhere rich.

Finish the dissolution walk - ground follows the firm, and hoist the duplicated HQ rule
items.author: Ben
items.design: Two loose ends the wave-2 review barrier found in BL-628, neither a defect today. (1) world::province_holder takes a CORP id via battle_system.cpp's field_held_by, and dissolve_into's inventory does not carry it. Entity ids are monotonic with no recycling, so a stale holder is inert rather than aliasing - but R4's wording is 'no dangling reference survives', and ground is PROPERTY, so it TRANSFERS. Now written into FINANCE.md's three-way rule, which also gained a fourth outcome, KEEP, for the historical record - history is not property and is never rewritten, which is the one place a reference to the erased corp survives on purpose. Extend the harness fixture to hold a province, since it currently never constructs one. (2) recompute_hq in corp_command.cpp DUPLICATES designate_hq/corp_home_body from corporation_generation.cpp, including kProjectedReachUnits = 2.5f - unavoidable at authoring because another slice owned that file in the same wave. Both have landed; the review verified them line-for-line identical. Hoist to a shared seam so they cannot drift.

items.title: charter_reach is computed at generation and silently zeroed on load
items.author: Ben
items.design: Found by the wave-2 review barrier. BL-638 added settlement_state::charter (a charter_reach), and w_settlement/r_settlement do not carry it. The omission is SYMMETRIC so the stream stays consistent and no version bump is owed - it is not a corruption bug. It is a LATENT one: the field is silently zeroed on load, which is benign only while the sole readers are generate_corporations and its harness, both of which run before any save exists. It becomes wrong the moment BL-627 (profitability ledger), BL-629 (rival acquisition) or the generation ledger reads charter off a LOADED world - and it will read as 'this world has no charter' rather than as an error. TWO HONEST ROUTES, pick one and say why: serialise it (a version bump, claimed through next_save_version.js), or RECOMPUTE it on load from the ladder it is derived from, which costs no format change and cannot drift from its source. The second is probably right, since charter_reach is a pure function of already-serialised state.

items.title: A demand injector that cannot price a basket entry must SAY SO, not skip it
items.author: Ben
items.design: THE MECHANISM THAT MADE TWO SEPARATE BUGS INVISIBLE ON THE SAME DAY, which is why it is an item rather than a note. inject_population_demand and inject_background_demand both SKIP a basket entry whose resource carries no market base price - silently, with no warning and no row anywhere. Consequences observed 2026-08-26: (1) BL-649's census read as having no background demand at all on its first run, and (2) tools/verify/spawn_solvency.cpp - whose own header says it loads world_gen.lua and did not - measured BL-635's entire spawn diagnosis in a world where background demand did not exist. Neither failed. Both just quietly answered a question about a different world. THE WORK: an injector that cannot price a basket entry must report it - a named diagnostic on the first occurrence, and a harness row that FAILS on a basket naming an unpriced good, since that combination is always either a missing script or an authoring error and is never intended. A basket entry is a STATEMENT that somebody wants the good; silently dropping it turns a design statement into a no-op. Cheap, and it protects every measurement the rest of Sprint 21 depends on.

items.title: The eighth field - a return sees the whole quarter, not just the money loop
items.author: Ben
items.design: Ben's ruling, 2026-08-26, on NR-655/NR-668 - option A of the three-way fork, and the measurement that forced it: a firm earning through mercenary contracts files a trailing_net IDENTICAL to a firm that earns nothing there, so BL-628's buyout undervalues it by exactly 640 credits (k 8.0 x the 80/quarter the record cannot see). Design in FINANCE.md section The eighth field. THE WORK: add `other` to quarterly_return = the whole-tick balance delta minus the money-loop net, and MOVE THE FILING from the end of apply_budget to after the tick's last balance mover - which is the part that needs care, since apply_budget does not own the tick and the headless harnesses call it directly. Then re-point corp_trailing_net at the mean of (net + other) so the buyout prices off the whole quarter. THREE PROPERTIES TO ASSERT: the seven flows still explain `net` unchanged; net+other telescopes EXACTLY over a run (the retain property extended from one function to the whole tick); and BL-628's own harness row that currently PINS the 640-credit blindness must be re-specified to pin the closure instead - do not delete it, invert it. `other` is deliberately NOT itemised: split into named lines it becomes a second budget breakdown competing with corp_budget, and the reason there is one accounting authority is that two of them disagree. Versions the save format.

items.title: A short pool buys on the market, up to a reservation ceiling
items.author: Ben
items.design: THE BLOCKER UNDER BL-641, AND PROBABLY UNDER FOUR MORE CHANNELS. Measured 2026-08-26: with building upkeep rates on, operating firms went 227 -> 19, because the goods drawn are produced 0.0 in band and a POOL DRAW never reaches market_component::demand - so the want never becomes a price, no rival scores the building that would supply it, and the sink starves itself. run_construction and run_processing already bid; run_unit_upkeep does not and carries the same latent defect. DESIGN-OWED, and the open question is Ben's because it widens FINANCE.md: should a goods draw place real demand on the market when the pool is short - and if so, does it BUY (spending credits, which makes upkeep a market participant) or merely SIGNAL (raising price without a transaction, which is cheaper but invents demand nobody pays for)? The first is coherent and expensive; the second is a thumb on the scale and should probably be refused on the same grounds the project refuses clamps. Until this is settled, BL-641's rates stay at 0.0 and every remaining channel (BL-643 infrastructure, BL-644 state, BL-645 research, BL-646 conflict) should be checked against property 3 before it is built, not after. SETTLED (Ben, 2026-08-26): 'Buy on the market, but at a threshold, buying is not allowed. This goes hand in hand with maximum and minimum prices for goods.' And ONE RULE FOR EVERY GOODS DRAW - unit upkeep takes the same shape, not a second one. Written into MARKETS.md section Settled: a short pool BUYS, up to a reservation ceiling. THE WORK: a short pool bids the shortfall into market_component::demand and pays for what it gets; above the ceiling it does not bid at all and the existing shortfall rule weakens the building (or unit) instead. The ceiling is authored in the PRICE BAND family beside floor_mult/ceil_mult, not in upkeep - it is a statement about what a good is worth paying, not about who is buying - and its value is MEASURED against the census and the operating-firm count, never guessed. It is the exact mirror of BL-386's seller-side floor_price: both sides may decline a trade, neither may dictate one. Turning BL-641's rates non-zero is gated on this landing.

items.title: Retune background-firm density upward against the corrected demand basis
items.author: Ben
items.design: Ben's ruling on NR-679, 2026-08-26: KEEP BL-640's fix, and retune density back up toward the old world. The fix is not in question - Pass 6 was chasing ~90% of a demand that included goods the ancient band cannot produce, so it added firms against a gap that could never close, and correcting it took the world from 584 buildings / 104 corps to 261 / 64. TWO LEVERS REACH THE SAME COUNT AND THEY MEAN DIFFERENT THINGS, which is the whole of this item: (a) RAISE PASS 6'S TARGET FRACTION above 0.90 - the world then deliberately OVERPRODUCES, which means gluts, prices pinned at the floor, and thinner margins for everyone; it reaches the count without anyone wanting more. (b) RAISE THE DEMAND BASKETS - the world CONSUMES more per head, so more firms are supported at the same ~90% ratio and prices hold. TRY (b) FIRST: it preserves what BL-640 established, and POPULATION.md already names the knob as an open item - the cost of living, how much it costs a head to live, deliberately unquantified. (a) is the fallback and should be recorded as a deliberate oversupply if taken. MEASURE BOTH with demand_census against the committed baseline plus the corp and operating-building counts, and report the price consequence - a density that is right only because everything is worthless is not right.

items.title: Decide what actually shapes background density - the ratio, or the per-resource cap
items.author: Ben
items.design: Raised by BL-655's measurement and by its novelty flag. Pass 6 is documented as stopping on a 0.90 production/demand ratio, described as 'an emergent measurement rather than an injected clearing constant' and 'a stop condition, not a firm-count budget'. MEASURED: the ratio NEVER BINDS on the worlds we generate. `per_resource_firm_cap = 8` binds on every demanded resource, so the count is exactly specialists + 8 x basket breadth - which reproduced 104, 64 and 56 corps exactly across three configurations. Its own comment still says 'provisional - measure, then pin'. The doc has been corrected to describe what the code does; what is OPEN is which behaviour is wanted. THREE READINGS: (a) the cap is the real design and the ratio is dead weight - pin the cap deliberately, say density is breadth-driven, and delete the ratio; (b) the ratio is the real design and the cap is an emergency brake set too low - raise it until the ratio binds, which restores the 'calibrated, not authored' property the doc claims; (c) both, with the cap as a genuine guard against a pathological basket. Note the consequence either way: under (a) density becomes a function of how many DIFFERENT goods are wanted, so every demand channel Sprint 21 adds moves the world's size - which may be a feature.

items.title: A firm underwater long enough exits - give interest the consequence it is supposed to have
items.author: Ben
items.design: MEASURED 2026-08-26 from Ben's own observation of the live build. Of 12 seeds, 3 clear with ZERO interest; the 9 that fail all dipped negative once and interest is then 43-60% of their whole loss, against an operating gap of only -24 to -40 cr/qtr. 1.02^80 = 4.9x over the warm start. The rate is not the defect - components.hpp's 'no insolvency consequence' is. A firm that would have died in year three trades for twenty and is handed to the player as wreckage. THE WORK: a firm underwater for N consecutive quarters EXITS - dissolved, or absorbed via BL-628's dissolve_into, which already moves holdings, pools, balance and returns and cancels the promises nobody is left to keep. N and the trigger are authored in economy.lua and MEASURED, not picked. DESIGN-OWED on three questions that are Ben's: (1) dissolve or absorb - absorption by a solvent neighbour is richer and reuses the buyout path, dissolution is simpler and leaves ground free; (2) does this run IN PLAY as well as in the pre-game, i.e. can the player's own corp fail - NR-670 already ruled a rival may not BUY the player out, and this is a different question about the player failing on their own account; (3) what happens to the ground and the workforce - a dissolved firm's tiles should probably become available rather than stay held. EXPECTED CONSEQUENCE, and the reason this is priority A: the field at seat time becomes self-selected for viability, so BL-630's shortlist floor should start being met instead of falling through to its fallback on 23 of 24 seeds.
